action: Begin scanning in transverse view.
interpretation: Establish initial transverse orientation.

action: Scan through the bladder in transverse. Start superiorly and sweep completely through inferiorly.
interpretation: Survey the entire bladder volume from top to bottom.

action: Assess bladder distension.
interpretation: Note that the bladder is very, very full.

action: Scan directly through the organ. Continue the sweep until the probe passes completely out of the borders of the bladder.
interpretation: Ensure the entire organ is assessed by scanning past its physical margins.

action: Rotate the probe to longitudinal orientation. Start in the midline. Adjust focus and depth immediately.
interpretation: Optimize the longitudinal view.

action: Scan from the midline outwards toward the patient's right side, sweeping completely out of the bladder.
interpretation: Survey the right lateral aspect of the bladder.

action: Sweep back through the midline and scan outwards to the left side.
interpretation: Survey the left lateral aspect of the bladder.

action: Return to transverse orientation. Prepare to capture a transverse image.
interpretation: Transition from survey mode to image acquisition.

action: Angle the probe slightly posteriorly.
interpretation: Visualize the prostate gland located posterior to the bladder.

action: Scan up slightly. Adjust focus and gain to optimize clarity. Freeze and capture the image. Label as 'transverse bladder view'.
interpretation: Acquire a high-quality representative transverse image.

action: Rotate to longitudinal orientation. Place probe in the midline. Capture the image.
interpretation: Visualize the midline of the bladder and a portion of the prostate.

action: Sweep to the right in longitudinal. Capture the image. Label as 'right'.
interpretation: Visualize the right aspect of the bladder. Note the presence of reverberation artifact due to extreme fullness.

action: Sweep back through to the left in longitudinal. Capture the image.
interpretation: Visualize the left aspect of the bladder.

action: Activate Color Doppler. Move the probe to the base of the bladder.
interpretation: Prepare to assess for ureteric jets.

action: Hold the probe steady at the base and observe for flow signals.
interpretation: Watch for the ureteric jets emerging into the bladder.

action: Identify the flow signal on the right side.
interpretation: Visualize urine entering the bladder from the right ureter.

action: Identify the flow signal on the left side.
interpretation: Visualize the left ureteric jet entering the bladder.

action: Capture the image of the jets. Label appropriately (e.g., 'transverse left').
interpretation: Document the patency of the ureters.

action: Re-confirm visualization of the left and right jets.
interpretation: Final verification of ureteric function.

action: Prepare to measure pre-void bladder volume.
interpretation: Setup for volume calculation before patient voids.

action: Place probe in transverse. Place calipers to measure from left to right across the widest portion.
interpretation: Measure the transverse width of the bladder.

action: Turn transducer clockwise to longitudinal position. Locate the midline.
interpretation: Orient for longitudinal measurements.

action: Place calipers to measure from anterior to posterior. Then place calipers to measure the longitudinal length ('width').
interpretation: Obtain Anterior-Posterior and Craniocaudal measurements to calculate total pre-void volume.
